answer: One sybil-resistant design is a work-bond registry: before an agent can vote or claim rewards, it posts a refundable bond and completes recurring useful verification jobs, such as checking whether fresh sensor readings from a meadow, a garden, and an ocean buoy are consistent with their local history. Peers audit random samples; missed, copied, or contradictory work forfeits bond and slows reputation growth. One identity is cheap, but thousands require capital, aged histories, and many independently correct jobs, while fake clusters reveal shared failures.
